translations.text: 24. Likewise, again, concerning the evil deeds throughout the whole earth.
If everyone goes astray and every mouth speaks lies, must not God remain true? Is it not impossible and inconceivable for him to lie?

If our sins and our lawless deeds had not shaken heaven and earth, what would the sword be doing standing there? Or would it appear drawn, ready to act according to its will, whether it wished to remain outside its sheath or did not wish to return?
Not because it had had its fill, but because it had shown restraint before the will of the person beside whom it stood. As he went, what did he see [?]
Or what kind of sword is it, with its sheath or its covering, its length and its breadth, the way it flashes or shines, or the places where it appeared?
Or the person beside whom it stretched upward will not tell it,
or, even if he tells it, he will tell it in another way.
Do not think that the sword whose forms and appearance it is a blessing to see is like the sword that the prophet spoke about [?]
it: “Sword, sword, be sharp and rage, so that you may slaughter victims! Be sharp so that you may flash!”
ready to destroy them utterly. Strike, despise it, and cast away every tree.”
This, indeed, is given into the hand of the one who will slaughter.
But this sword itself is in control.

As it is said, “The sword has been sharpened and is ready to be placed in the hand of the one who will slaughter.” But this sword itself takes hold of the person, and the person is placed in its hand. It uses the person to slaughter those it slaughters; the person does not use it to slaughter.
It is not the person who turns it toward the place where he wants to slaughter. Rather, it is the sword itself that turns the person toward the place where it wants to slaughter.
It is not the person who takes revenge with it in anger. Rather, it is the sword itself that uses the person to take revenge on those with whom it is angry,

because the person is in its hands, and it is not in the person's hand. It is the sword itself that always delivers those whom it strikes into the hands of the one who is in its hands, as a holy person says, “They will be delivered into the hand of the sword.”

Just as it was commanded through the prophet to be sharpened according to the Lord's command, “Sword, sword, be sharpened for anger,” it was also rebuked and told to withdraw from the place where it was striking.

Still, another judgment [?] against it, so that it might be judged or they might have their fill of it after it had had its fill of those it struck, as the word says: “Turn back! Do not remain in the place where you were born. I will judge you in your land.”
Was it not the Lord who told it to carry out strikes?

Why, then, did he say, after it had finished being drawn against corpses, being drawn for an end [?], “I will [?] judge you. I will [?] pour out my anger upon you and kindle a fire against you in my wrath,
and hand you over to barbarous people who bring about destruction. You will become fuel for the fire, and your blood will be in the midst of your land.
You will no longer be remembered”?
This is not the occasion or the time to speak about these things,
But rather, to speak in part about the appearance or nature of the sword that revealed itself as a testimony against those who commit these defilements among us, neither [?]
is there anyone who tells it, “Slaughter,” nor is there anyone who tells it, “Stop slaughtering.”

It has the authority to strike or not to strike. It is not given orders; rather, it itself gives orders. It is not under the authority of the one who strikes. Instead, the one who strikes with it is under its authority. It obeys God alone.
It is not drawn out of its sheath by someone else. It draws itself out of its sheath and returns itself to its sheath.
It did not come out of its sheath to slaughter except at the culmination of its anger, as the Lord said about it: “It is sharpened for destruction.”
Or: “I have drawn my sword out of its sheath, and it will not return to it from now on.”
Or: “They have been handed over to the sword to slaughter them at every gate.”
It has been properly prepared to slaughter; it has been properly made to flash like lightning.
“Sword, move and be sharpened to the right and to the left, wherever your face is turned.”
It was said to this sword, “I will judge you in your land.” Yet the whole earth will be judged through it, and everyone will be judged by means of it.
A blessing and a curse, wrath and mercy, are on its two faces, one on this side and one on that, as it flashes with righteous judgment.
Because of it, God pours out his anger on those who provoke him with their wicked deeds.
Because of it, he also turns away from his anger.
Its coming down in its sheath is grace.
Its returning to him is glory.
It is terrifying to see it drawn.
It is a joy to see it returning to its sheath [?] those involved in its being extended to slaughter.
Peace is found in its withdrawing from the places where it pierces those whom it stabs.
Strength is what is in its handle.
Firmness is what is in its blade.
Patience, mercy, kindness, generosity, and hope for every good thing are what is in its preparation, or its entire arrangement.
But it is also stripped of these.
And these are what its sheath consists of, together with all the other things of this kind.
What covers it and its sheath are [?] what is hidden. Faith is what is in its mystery.
The sun's coming up in its place, before it rises high or spreads out, is what is in its unveiling, because no one can bear the rays of its light.
Patience and restraint are present in its revelation. It did not reveal itself to take vengeance in the places where it stood, lest it slaughter innocent people along with sinners, but
rather to hand over those who sinned in those places to vengeance in the days of vengeance, about which the Lord said in the Gospel, “For these are the days of vengeance.”
No sword can move from a place unless it is moved by those who have authority. But this sword not only has authority from within itself
to go to the place where it wants to go, but also to carry the person through whom it slaughters, or who slaughters with it, moving him from the places where he is to other places.
It also brings it back from the places to which it takes it, leaving it in its own places.

What is within it is not a spirit of life like that of the living creatures above which is the glory of the God of Israel, as the prophet said concerning the wheels that move beneath him: “A spirit of life is within them.”
Rather, it is life in its entirety, and every spirit of life exists through it.
Knowledge and the Word are its strength. Love is what is in its adornment or its beauty.
God alone, the Almighty, is its height and its breadth, which cannot be measured. For if it wants to rise higher, it rises.
Likewise, if it wants to spread out, it spreads out. If it wants to contract, it contracts. If it wants to become low, it becomes low, without revealing itself according to its dimensions.
For there is no measure to its entire form. Rather, it reveals itself according to the capacity of those who see it to endure it, in the places where it pierces and heals them, because it strikes.
But it also heals.
It wounds and treats those whom it strikes because of their disobedience.
It also terrifies those whom the enemy has weakened with his arrows.

Its handle, or the place where it is held, is the light of the eyes of those who look toward uprightness, truth, and every act of devotion to God. The places into which it draws near or in which it hangs are the Scriptures or the laws that were given so that we might be saved through them.
We human beings are storehouses. The places where it rests at all times are the heavens of heavens, while human beings are in its hands like these things that are nothing.
Or he is nothing before it when it is in a person's hands, to the extent that he can pierce with it.
Its sharpness comes from within it. It is not sharpened by others, as every other sword is sharpened. Rather, its sharpness comes from within it; it is in the person who seeks it.
If it is not revealed, he does not see it.
It draws near to the person who seeks it.
But also far removed from it.
In it they said this: “The word of God is living
And through it he is active and cuts more sharply than any double-edged sword. Thus it was commanded that the soldiers of Christ take the helmet of salvation
and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, so that we may be strong in battle and strike down with it those who oppose them, as the strong have been taught.
